newsitem.title: USA: New York Times says Times, Globe ads rise.
newsitem.headline: New York Times says Times, Globe ads rise.

text.p: The New York Times Co on Monday said April and year-to-date ad volumes at the New York Times and Boston Globe newspapers are up from 1996 while volume at its Regional Newspaper Group remains flat.

The company said April advertising inches at the Times rose 4.1 percent to 406,300 inches. April volume at the Globe rose 3.3 percent to 297,500 inches, while volume at the Regional group was down 0.5 percent to 1.5 million inches.

The company said year-to-date volume at the Times is up 3.3 percent to 1.3 million inches. Globe volume is up 4.3 percent to just over 1 million inches. Regional Newspapers volume is up 0.6 percent to 5.2 million.

April's strongest performers at the Times were national and classified ads, which rose 6.2 percent and 11.2 percent, respectively. Top movers at the Globe also were national and classifieds, which rose 9.1 percent and 7 percent, respectively.
National and classified ads both led the year-to-date increases at both papers.
At the Regional group, legal ads were off 33.7 percent, and national ads were down 10.6 percent in April. For the year, national ads are up 10.6 percent.
